title: Cross-tenant quarantine and immutable-region ledgers for analytics residency enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As Redwood expands regional deployments, we must ensure usage analytics (events, aggregated metrics, and raw ingestion) obey tenant residency constraints while preserving the console's global observability. Current pipeline fans events to a single global topic and relies on downstream filters, which creates exposure and complicates compliance for regulated tenants.

Goal: Implement tenant-aware replication fencing with an immutable region-ledger per tenancy that enforces write locality, regulates cross-region mirroring, provides deterministic replay gating, and exposes residency-safe read APIs for the Console. The system should support: (1) tenant affinity for writes, (2) policy-driven conditional mirroring to secondary regions, (3) immutable region-ledgers for tamper-evident audit and replay, and (4) transparent fallbacks when local capacity is constrained.

Scope and approach:
- Ingest layer: add a tenant residency classifier step to the upstream collector (Console-ingest service) which stamps events with resolved residency_policy and target_region_set. This lookup uses a cached Residency Config store with TTL and watch semantics.
- Replication fencing: implement a write fencing token issued per-tenant-region by the Residency Coordinator service. Writers without a valid token for a region are rejected or routed to policy fallback. The coordinator supports lease renewal and emergency evacuation signals.
- Immutable region-ledgers: for each tenant-region pair create an append-only ledger (S3+Glue catalog + object manifest or dedicated regional write-ahead log) that records event segments and manifests with signed checksums. Ledgers support deterministic replay to rehydrate regional materialized views and are scoped to retention requirements.
- Mirroring policy engine: declarative policies (no-mirror, delayed-mirror, mirror-with-redaction) drive which tenants/events are mirrored. Mirroring is implemented as region-aware stream connectors with watermarking to avoid out-of-order reconciliation issues.
- Read APIs / Console backend: expose residency-aware aggregation endpoints (region-scoped and global-safe view) with query rewriting that only includes data permitted by policy. Include a residency badge in UI responses and a per-tenant audit endpoint for manifest and ledger provenance.
- Security & compliance: all region-ledgers encrypted with tenant-specific KMS keys (customer-managed where configured). Audit logs capture lease issuance and mirroring decisions for compliance reviews.
- Failure modes & evacuation: define evacuation protocol when a region becomes unavailable: (a) emergency read-only fallback to last-known ledger snapshot, (b) staging queue for replay when target region recovers, (c) automatic switch to approved secondary region only if policy permits.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Residency Config store and classifier: rollout to ingestion edge (staged in us-west-2) with feature flag and 2-week shadow monitoring.
2) Residency Coordinator & fencing tokens: internal alpha for a small set of high-compliance tenants; validate lease durability and renewal under load.
3) Immutable ledgers: create regional ledgers for 10 pilot tenants, run parity checks against global pipeline, and build reconciliation tooling.
4) Mirroring policy engine: allow tenant admins to select policy in Console (UI work tracked in PM).
5) Gradual expansion: increase tenant coverage while monitoring replay success rate, latency, and cost.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- Metric: % of tenant writes accepted by region (target 99.95% for pinned regions).
- Metric: mirror lag P95 (target < 30s for near-real-time policies, < 24h for delayed).
- Metric: ledger parity checks success rate and checksum mismatch rate (target 99.999%).
- Alerting: fence-token issuance failures, classifier cache misses > threshold, mirror connector errors, and ledger write failures.

Testing and verification:
- Integration tests that simulate regional outage and verify evacuation/replay semantics.
- Chaos tests that forcibly revoke fencing tokens and assert safe read behavior in Console.
- Pen tests for KMS key handling and ledger access APIs.

Open decisions and trade-offs:
- Data store for ledgers: S3 object manifests vs regional append-only DB. S3 is cost effective and durable but complicates low-latency replay; DB gives lower-latency replay but higher operational cost. Decision: start with S3-ledgers and pilot a Cassandra/Storage-Node-backed ledger for tenants needing sub-second replay.
- Granularity of fencing token: per-tenant-region vs per-tenant-region-shard. We will begin with per-tenant-region for simplicity; if hotspots arise we'll introduce shard tokens.
- UI surface: minimal residency badge + drilldown audit for MVP; richer per-route residency visualizations in subsequent cycles.

Documentation and artifacts:
- Confluence design: /confluence/redwood/analytics-residency-ledger-design (link placeholder).
- Initial PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4123 (ingest classifier).
- Prototype dashboard: Grafana: rwd.analytics.residency.pilot (read-only link).

Success criteria:
- Pilot tenants (n=10) fully served with region-pinned writes and mirrored copies where policy allowed without any compliance violations.
- Zero unencrypted ledger writes in pilot.
- Mirror lag P95 within policy limits and resolution playbooks validated.

Next steps (actionable):
- Carlos: spin up Residency Coordinator prototype and implement token API (owner).
- Linus Zhou: add classifier hook into Console-ingest and publish residency metadata in the event envelope (assignee: Linus for ingestion work).
- PM: create tenant-facing policy editing flow in Console (blocked by backend toggles).
